Use Tier 2: replace the uniform cumulative-taste pooling with learned, recency-aware causal attention inside the existing SASRec network. Focus on model_design and training_evaluation; keep the data splits, sampled-softmax objective, and training settings fixed for a controlled experiment. The current model improves CDs_and_Vinyl substantially but trails the baseline on the other three categories, suggesting that its history representation may transfer unevenly across domains. Uniform pooling gives every observed item equal influence, which can dilute recent purchase intent with older, unrelated interests.

At each supervised sequence position, use the current transformer state as a query over preceding item embeddings, with a jointly learned relative-distance bias controlling recency. Mask padding and future positions, then pass the attention-pooled history through the existing taste projection and fusion gate. This lets one network learn when to emphasize recent interactions and when to retrieve older relevant interests. Train exactly one independent model per category and retain one validation-selected checkpoint, without averaging or external scoring components.

Select checkpoints using macro-average validation HR@10 with the fixed seed-42 protocol, 200 users per category, and 99 unique negative candidates. Update the predictor writer to reconstruct the modified network and preserve identical history processing and dataset routing during host evaluation. Keep DATA_DIR as os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], write artifacts beneath the trial directory, and leave test inference and evaluation to the host.
